answer: An AI receptionist is a voice agent that answers your business phone, understands what the caller needs and acts on it: answering questions from your own information, booking appointments, taking messages or transferring the call. body:
Why Australian businesses are switching to an AI receptionist

Missed calls are lost work. A patient who reaches voicemail books with the clinic down the road. A homeowner with a burst pipe calls the next plumber on the list. A buyer enquiring about a listing moves on to another agent. Most small businesses can’t afford a full-time receptionist, and even those that have one can’t answer two calls at once, cover lunch breaks or pick up at 9pm.

An AI receptionist closes those gaps. It answers on the first ring, every time, and handles the routine calls that make up most of a typical day: booking requests, opening hours, directions, pricing you’ve approved and simple account questions. Your staff then spend their phone time on the calls that genuinely need a person.

What our AI receptionist does on every call

  1. Answers with your business name in a natural Australian English voice, and tells callers they are speaking with an AI assistant.
  2. Works out why they’re calling, whether that’s a new booking, a change, a quote request, a complaint or an emergency.
  3. Answers questions from a knowledge base built from your own services, prices, policies and FAQs.
  4. Books, moves or cancels appointments directly in your calendar or practice software, checking real availability.
  5. Sends an SMS confirmation with the time, address and anything the caller needs to bring.
  6. Logs a summary of the call in your CRM or emails it to the right person.
  7. Transfers the call to a staff member’s mobile when it is urgent, sensitive or outside what the AI should handle.

AI receptionist vs answering service vs voicemail

VoicemailHuman answering serviceAI receptionist
Availability24/7, but callers often hang upSet hours, or extra cost after hours24/7, several calls at once
Books appointmentsNoSometimes, by message to youYes, directly in your calendar
Knows your businessNoLimited scriptTrained on your own information
Call recordsAudio onlyWritten messageSummary and transcript in your CRM
Handover to staffCallback laterMessage or transferLive transfer with context

Many businesses use both: the AI receptionist handles routine calls around the clock, and a person picks up anything it transfers.

Who uses an AI receptionist

  • Clinics and allied health: physio, dental, chiro, psychology and GP practices that need bookings, reschedules and after-hours call handling. See AI for healthcare.
  • Trades and home services: plumbers, electricians and builders who are on the tools when the phone rings. See AI for trades.
  • Real estate agencies: inspection bookings, appraisal requests and tenant calls. See AI for real estate.
  • Professional services: law, accounting and consulting firms that want every enquiry captured and screened.

Connects to the systems you already use

The AI receptionist works with your current phone number through call forwarding, or on a new Australian number. It connects to calendars such as Google Calendar and Microsoft 365, practice and job software such as Cliniko and ServiceM8, and CRMs including HubSpot, Zoho and GoHighLevel. If your booking system has an API, we can usually connect to it. For outbound calls like reminders and quote follow-ups, pair it with an AI voice agent.

Privacy, transparency and control

Phone calls carry personal information, so every receptionist we build is designed around the Privacy Act 1988 and the OAIC’s guidance on privacy and commercially available AI products. Callers are told they are speaking with an AI, recording and transcription notices are set up to suit your state, and call data is stored in your systems with retention periods you choose.

You stay in control of what the AI can say and do. It never quotes prices you haven’t approved, never gives clinical, legal or financial advice, and always offers a way to reach a person. This follows the “maintain human control” practice in the Australian Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption.

How we set up your AI receptionist

  1. Free AI audit: we review your call volumes, peak times and the questions callers ask most.
  2. Call design: we write the greeting, booking rules, transfer rules and the answers it can give.
  3. Build and connect: we connect your number, calendar and CRM, and load your knowledge base.
  4. Test calls: your team calls it with real scenarios, including awkward ones, and we refine.
  5. Go live and improve: we review a sample of calls every month and send a report on calls handled, bookings made and transfers.

Not sure an AI receptionist is the right first step? Compare it with our other AI agents, or start with AI consulting.
faqs: Can an AI receptionist use my existing phone number?
Yes. Calls can forward from your current number to the AI receptionist all the time, only after hours, or only when your line is busy. You can also use a new Australian number.
Will callers know they are talking to an AI?

Yes. We recommend the receptionist tells callers it is an AI assistant at the start of the call, and it always offers a way to reach a person. This builds trust and suits Australian guidance on transparency.
What happens with urgent or difficult calls?
You set the rules. Emergencies, complaints, sensitive topics and anything the AI is unsure about are transferred live to a staff member, or a detailed message is sent to the right person immediately.
How much does an AI receptionist cost in Australia?

Cost depends on call volume, the systems it connects to and how many call types it handles. We quote a fixed set-up price in AUD after a free audit, then a monthly fee covering calls, hosting, monitoring and improvements.
Can it book into my practice or job management software?
Usually, yes. We connect to calendars such as Google and Microsoft 365 and to software including Cliniko and ServiceM8. If your system has an API or online booking, we can normally integrate with it.
